extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and PIs (biomedical researchers) seeking funding strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and explanatory notes about the new NIH 'competitive, but not discussed' (ND-C) designation, its relation to enhanced triage, and practical strategies (especially contacting Program Officers) for applicants who receive this outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'competitive but not discussed' designation
rubrics_metrics.description: This new designation is supposed to be applied to the ~middle third of proposals based on average preliminary impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launched when triage was increased to ~70%; may or may not be printed on the summary statement. It identifies applications that are in the middle third (i.e., better than the bottom third triaged out, but not in the top discussed set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced triage (≈70% triage rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Move to triage ~70% of proposals in a study section, instead of the prior ~50% rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 70% triage change created space for the ND-C designation. The author speculates CSR may make 70% triage the new normal and that the ND-C designation may persist accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program staff latitude to pick up ND proposals for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: In theory this permits broader latitude for Program staff to pick up a ND, competitive for funding via exception pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes Program could technically fund anything that did not get a 'Not Recommended for Further consideration' and that not funding ND proposals was more cultural/traditional than a legal prohibition. Under the new regime, 'exception pay' terminology may be phased out as Program departs from strict ordering by peer review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary applicant strategy: contact your Program Officer (PO) after receiving the summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your number one strategy is to contact your PO after you get your summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is increasingly important given the possibility of no published NOSI and increased permission for Program to ignore the order of review. POs are the ones navigating internal policies (e.g., geographic diversity) and may be the only practical route to advocate for ND-C pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic diversity as a possible affirmative-action consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole remaining broad quota based affirmative action policy mentioned is 'geographical diversity'—red state institutions will be prioritized for awards in some way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance from leadership on this is vague; no NOFO or concrete policy was observed. Applicants who qualify (e.g., at red state institutions) might raise this with their PO, but specifics are unclear and uptake appears limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of ND-C designation on the summary statement and reviewer implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Author thought the designation would not be on the summary statement, but recent tweetage suggests it will be. If it ends up on the summary statement, reviewers of the amended version will have this info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may or may not change reviewer behavior because reviewers have had access to criterion scores for years and can estimate overall standing from those scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical funding pathway for competitive ND applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rough funding sequence: added to the slate presented to Advisory Council by Program; Approved by Advisory Council; Selected post-AC by the Program process that ends with the IC Director’s say so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ND-C proposals would follow the same broad administrative pathway as other applications when Program decides to pick them up; contact with PO is the route to be considered for that pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation about likelihood of ND-C pickups
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobody is very hopeful that ND-C proposals will be picked up in any significant numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should set realistic expectations; while ND-C designation creates a theoretical route to funding, actual pickup rates may remain low.
